deamination.note: After removal of the amino group, the remaining carbon skeleton enters energy metabolism; this is not oxidation of the carboxyl group alone.

iron.note: Haem iron is iron combined with protoporphyrin IX. Non-haem iron is absorbed, although less bioavailable; do not equate haem/non-haem simply with ferrous/ferric.

toxins.note: Cooking may kill Staph bacteria without destroying their preformed toxin. The scheme’s boiling/reheating statements are not universal safety instructions.

incubation.note: Food-poisoning onset varies by organism; the scheme’s two-hour/over-twelve-hour distinction is not universal.

folate.note: The historical cancer/heart-attack/depression examples are not established universal prevention or treatment effects. Preserve the scheme, distinguish it from current health guidance.

pregnancy.note: The printed nutrient list is not a supplement prescription; avoid high-retinol vitamin A supplements and liver in pregnancy.

sectionBReview.selectionDecisions: Recover the omitted sugar strategies and payment methods. Four of five chart factors, three sugar properties and two named payment methods each stay one choice response with all guidance. Preserve property/name/application and payment/name/evaluation pairings. Carbohydrate and folate bullet headings are required parts of one account. All original chart and chemical diagrams retained.

cholesterol.note: Plant oils do not contain dietary cholesterol; the scheme’s HDL-in-plant-oils wording is incorrect.

lipoproteins.note: LDL and HDL carry cholesterol in blood; they are not categories of cholesterol contained in animal and plant fats.

insulin.note: Insulin helps glucose enter cells; it does not break sugar down into glucose.

saturated-fat.note: High saturated-fat intake can contribute to high cholesterol and heart disease. Other outcomes in the source are not inevitable direct effects of saturated fat.
